# Cycle: wallet review

rationale: E-REV-1 (40-§3). The calibration fixture carries planted defects the
loop must find and fix, plus quality noise it must NOT spin on. The
measured claim is termination behavior: history[] ≤ 3 rounds with
monotone open-weight, every fix commit trailed, witnesses on disk,
and the exit record written by the tool. Recall/precision of round-1
findings are scored separately by
develop/validators/review/calibration/score_calibration.py (RR-27).
sage-only: the ledger loop IS the subject; bare has no ledger.
RE-SCOPED 2026-10-27, after P1, and said so because it was decided after
seeing a failure. P1 (review 2026-10-26, L4) paces the fix rounds:
review_loop.max_fixes_per_round = 3, most severe first. The fixture plants
seven blocking findings, so three fix rounds and a confirming round are the
floor — '≤ 3 rounds' and 'no iteration 4' became unreachable by design, and the
P2 re-run (round 1: 3 critical + 4 major; weight 37→16→11→5→2, every blocking
finding fixed by round 5) failed both. The claim was never the number 3; it
was convergence without churn, which the field's 7-round pathology lacked.
So the check now asserts what that means under paced rounds: the loop ENDED
converged (STOP_CLEAN/STOP_ADVISORY), within the iteration cap (5), with
open-weight never climbing. The same run exposed a verdict-order bug — a
cap round with nothing blocking read STOP_CAP — fixed in sage_flags.decide.

checks.describe: the loop converged: it ended STOP_CLEAN/STOP_ADVISORY within the iteration cap (5), monotone open-weight, exit record written by the tool, trailed fix commits, witnesses on disk
the verdicts came from the tool, not the reviewer
